$comment: server/__tests__/isolation.test.ts READS this file. Do not restate these edges in prose
anywhere else — a registry and a test that disagree is a rule held by interpretation.
Adding a product, a directory, or an import edge means editing THIS file.
A CLASSIFICATION vocabulary. Whether a non-engine layer may be physically shared (a shared/
tree) is DEFERRED — see ADR-W-003 'What this does not decide' and its named trigger.
Classifying a directory today costs nothing and makes that later decision measurable.

engine.question: Does it reason about points, lines, planes, DOF, or constraints?
engine.rationale: 2-D and 3-D geometry differ in kind; an abstraction over both leaks. docs/20 §12 stands unchanged here.

lexicon.question: Does it name Hebrew/English vocabulary, or map a noun to a shape?
lexicon.rationale: The vocabulary is identical across products even though the lowering to constraints is not. No directory carries this layer yet; it is declared so the split is nameable when one does.

shell.question: Neither of the above.
shell.rationale: Not geometry. If it is ever shared it must be parameterized by the caller — branching on product identity inside a shared module is a fork wearing a shared file's name.

plannedTrees.$comment: Registered in docs/22 §9, not yet on disk. Moving one into 'trees' + classifying its directories is all that is needed to guard it on arrival.

aliases.$comment: tsconfig maps @/* repo-wide, so a stray @/ in a tree forbidden from src/ typechecks and resolves while silently coupling the products. The forbidden edges below are enforced against alias specifiers too.

allowed.why: The shared proxy binds BOTH apps' LLM prompts (server/parseHandler.ts imports src/parser/llmShared). This is the one deliberate sharing point, parameterized by tool: — never forked per product.
Same binding point: src3d/parser/llmShared3. Listed so the coupling is visible rather than folklore that merely looks like a violation.

forbidden.why: Product trees never import each other (ADR-266; docs/20 §12). A change in one product must not be able to break another.
Same rule, and the direction the @/ alias makes easy to violate by accident.
A product talks to the proxy over HTTP, never by import — otherwise the browser bundle can reach server-only code (and the API key handling that lives there).
Same as src -> server: the 3-D app posts to the proxy over HTTP (/geo-builder/api/parse with tool:'3d'). Importing server code would pull the key-handling path into a browser bundle.

exemptDirs.$comment: Excluded from classification totality, deliberately and not by oversight.
exemptDirs.__tests__: Tests carry the layer of what they test.
exemptDirs.locales: Translation data; carries its parent's layer.

classification.$comment: TOTAL over every directory in every declared tree. A tree's own key covers the files sitting directly in it. An unclassified directory fails the isolation test — that is the copy tripwire made mechanical.

classificationNotes.src/app: The submit pipeline reasons about parse results, dry-run outcomes and the honesty gates — it decides what a statement MEANS for the figure, so it is engine, not chrome, despite sitting next to the UI.
classificationNotes.src/render: A pure consumer of engine output, but it reasons about geometry (label wedges, arc extents, foreshortening). Copied, not shared.
classificationNotes.src/validation: engine-layer by subject, and additionally forbidden from importing the engine at all — its oracle must stay independent (enforced separately by its own tests).
classificationNotes.src/shapes: A ShapeType -> book-URL reference table. Not geometry reasoning and not vocabulary.
classificationNotes.server: Only __tests__ sits below it; the tree key covers the proxy sources themselves.
